business_ops.seasonality: Two statements are printed, and the RHP does not reconcile them. (1) MD&A, section 'SEASONALITY OF BUSINESS' (affirmative nil): "Our business is not seasonal in nature." (2) Risk Factors, CDMO risk factor, forward-looking: "Seasonality - We expect to in future experience an increase in shipments made to our customers in the last quarter of our financial year from January to March as this corresponds to the start of the financial year for most of our customers who operate on a calendar year basis, where they typically conduct their capacity planning for the year and purchase more quantities of product from us resulting in generally more invoices raised in the relevant quarter, or an increase in the value of these invoices. As a result of such seasonal fluctuations, our revenue and cash flow from operations may fluctuate due to the increase in demand for our products during the fourth quarter of our financial year. Further, as a result of the above, our quarter on quarter financial results may not be comparable or a meaningful indicator of our future performance." This second statement is expressly about the CDMO business and is framed as an expectation for the future, not a historical pattern.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration: "Our broad capabilities are enabled by conversion of commodity plant-based derivative inputs (farm/microbe-to-pharmacy approach) and work with diverse microbial strains such as bacteria, fungi, yeast and algae to convert into high value steroid and hormonal pre-cursors. This supports backward integration and underpins our 'farm/microbe-to-pharmacy' approach. This integration allows us to make strategic, cost-effective 'make versus buy' decisions for key starting materials (KSMs) for over 80% of our products by revenue, thereby reducing external dependence for sourcing intermediates from other geographies. We are among the few backward-integrated Indian and global manufacturers capable of producing in-house corticosteroid and hormone precursors, as of March 31, 2026. (Source: F&S Report)" Fermentation capabilities span four modalities: (i) biotransformation of soy-derived sterols to corticosteroid and hormone pre-cursors, with in-house control over each step from raw material to final API production; (ii) classical fermentation for pipeline APIs; (iii) recombinant protein expression technologies for GLP-1 and Insulins; and (iv) precision fermentation and synthetic biology for nutraceuticals and food applications. Forward integration: "We have strategically invested in forward integration to complement our API and fermentation strengths with capabilities in technically complex injectables. Our complex injectables platform is centered on double chamber vials (DCVs) and differentiated drug device combinations, including double chamber bags (DCBs), and double chamber syringes (DCSs). We are one of the first generics companies globally to successfully develop DCV through backward integration, by relying on in-house materials and not imports, for Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate injection and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate." Residual external dependence: "Our principal raw materials include phytosterols and certain fermentation-based and semi-synthetic intermediates, as KSMs for our APIs. We procure such raw materials from our suppliers based on purchase orders" and "do not enter into any long-term agreements with our suppliers." opportunities: Biologics capacity expansion at the Ujjain Facility with a dedicated 14 KL fermentation unit (two reactors of 7 KL each) to meet growing demand for GLP-1 and Insulin.

Complex injectables commercialisation: Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate DCVs with an expected launch in Fiscal 2027 and a combined US market size of USD 288 million; the Company is in discussions with global specialty pharmaceutical companies for licensing agreements. (Source: F&S Report)

Pipeline products developed under the Section 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway of the U.S. Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act are estimated to have an addressable market of USD 890 million in 2025 globally, expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.7% between 2025 and 2026F. (Source: F&S Report)

Scale-up of CDMO offerings across the three interlinked differentiated platform technologies, leveraging multi-scale fermenters that support both high-volume and low-volume fermentation-based products.

India fermentation-outsourcing opportunity: the Company states its 700 KL fermentation capacity makes it one of India's largest industrial-scale fermentation capacities, in a market where CMOs and CDMOs dominate the outsourcing landscape. (Source: F&S Report)

China+1 supply-chain diversification: backward integration gives make-versus-buy flexibility for approximately 80% of the product portfolio, reducing dependence on China for intermediates. (Source: F&S Report)

Expansion beyond pharmaceuticals into nutraceuticals and alternative proteins through collaboration agreements, and exploration of food and specialty chemicals, including clean-label precision-fermentation based food products.

Structural demand drivers cited for the Company's end-markets: rising global prevalence of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases driving corticosteroid demand, and expanding hormone API demand from reproductive health, metabolic disorder and hormone replacement therapies.

Stated market entry barriers in double-chamber technology (complex manufacturing and specialised infrastructure, high capital investment, stringent regulatory requirements, and IP and licensing constraints) that limit the field of entrants. (Source: Frost & Sullivan)
R&D pipeline includes multiple proprietary and classical fermentation APIs and development of a generic version of Premarin. (Source: F&S Report)
strengths: Global leadership in corticosteroid and steroidal hormone APIs: global volume market share of 38.2% in corticosteroid and 23.8% in steroidal-hormone APIs as of Fiscal 2026; only Indian and global company present across the top 10 corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs in Fiscal 2026. (Source: F&S Report)

Product portfolio of over 60 corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs spanning sterile and non-sterile formats, covering 90% of the market; over 50% volume market share in Hydrocortisone (80.1%), Testosterone (76.4%) and Methylprednisolone (76.0%) in Fiscal 2026. (Source: F&S Report)

As of March 31, 2026, generated the highest revenue among Indian API manufacturers from the sale of corticosteroid and steroidal hormone APIs in the three preceding Fiscals, having backward integrated into in-house corticosteroid and hormone precursors.
Differentiated chemistry capabilities enabling manufacture of APIs and products with up to 400 synthesis steps validated under cGMP.

Regulatory credentials: 43 DMFs registered with the US FDA and 23 CEPs from the EDQM as of March 31, 2026; Rau and Pithampur facilities accredited by US FDA, WHO-GMP, EU-GMP and others; 11 regulatory-agency inspections and audits from over 90 customers successfully completed over the last three Fiscals.

Vertically integrated 'farm/microbe-to-pharmacy' platform with maximum fermentation capacity of 700 KL (including the commissioned Ujjain Facility and Mhow Facility of certain Subsidiaries), 584.67 MT aggregate maximum chemical synthesis capacity and 20 million vials for complex injectables as of March 31, 2026.
Make-versus-buy flexibility for KSMs of over 80% of the product portfolio by revenue, reducing dependence on external sources for intermediates and imports from other geographies.

Long-standing customer base: over 200 customers in more than 40 countries as of March 31, 2026, with more than 50 domestic and 150 export customers; 101 new customers added in Fiscal 2026 versus 96 in Fiscal 2025 and 89 in Fiscal 2024; average relationship tenure of more than ten years for both the top five and top ten customers.

Low customer churn and high switching costs arising from DMF/CEP requirements, product-specific validation, bioequivalence studies and regulatory approvals; two of the top five customers as of March 31, 2026 are steroidal-hormone innovators. (Source: F&S Report)
Three dedicated R&D centres in Indore, Madhya Pradesh as of March 31, 2026, staffed by over 86 organic-chemistry scientists, 14 complex-injectables scientists and 39 biotechnology scientists.

Among the first generics companies globally to develop double-chamber vial technology (DCVs) through backward integration, for Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate injection and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate injections, which have a combined US market size of US$ 288 million. (Source: F&S Report)
Among the few Indian companies with multi-scale fermenters, enabling both high-volume and low-volume fermentation-based products and supporting CDMO services across production volumes.
Environmentally sustainable operating practices including flow chemistry for Progesterone production, renewable energy usage and zero-liquid discharge systems.
threats: Highly competitive market in both API manufacturing and CDMO; competitors may allocate more resources to development, promotion and sale of products, may have lower production costs and be better positioned to endure lower prices to gain market share, and may possess greater technical, manufacturing, R&D, sales, marketing and financial resources. (Risk Factor 8)

US trade measures: on September 25, 2025 the United States announced that effective October 1, 2025, 100% tariffs would be imposed on all branded / patented pharmaceutical products and their associated APIs manufactured outside the United States; in February 2026 an India-US interim bilateral framework reduced the reciprocal tariff on Indian-origin goods to 18% from 50%. Revenue from the United States represented 13.12%, 4.02% and 8.97% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. (Risk Factor 4)

Loss of market share in products where the Company holds over 50% volume share (Hydrocortisone 80.1%, Testosterone 76.4%, Methylprednisolone 76.0% in Fiscal 2026) may adversely affect the business. (Risk Factor 39)

Dependence on raw material procurement from countries including China and the United States; adverse developments in those countries or in the laws governing imports could disrupt raw material supply. (Risk Factor 9)

Extensive and continuously evolving regulation from governmental and international authorities; manufacturing facilities are subject to periodic inspections and audits by regulatory authorities and by customers, and any manufacturing or quality control failure may trigger regulatory action and reputational damage. (Risk Factors 2 and 12)
Product liability exposure if products, or other products containing the Company's corticosteroid or steroidal-hormone APIs, cause or are alleged to cause harm. (Risk Factor 15)

Foreign exchange risk: revenue from external customers outside India represented 67.04%, 55.19% and 59.97% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, exposing export receivables and inventory cost to rate fluctuations. (Risk Factors 3 and 51)

Dependence on the ability to develop and commercialise new products in a timely manner, and risk that changes in technology render current technologies obsolete or require substantial investment. (Risk Factors 10 and 50)
Hazardous activities and materials involved in operations, with risk of accidents, environmental damage and consequent liability. (Risk Factor 11)
Third-party supply chain risk in the supply of products, and risk from manufacture, distribution and sale of counterfeit or falsified products. (Risk Factors 44 and 66)
Reliance on the F&S Report, which was prepared exclusively for the Offer and commissioned and paid for by the Company, for industry and market-share information. (Risk Factor 55)
weaknesses: Revenue concentrated in APIs: sale of APIs constituted 96.07%, 99.10% and 100.00% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively; the top five APIs constituted 62.27%, 63.16% and 60.37% of revenue from operations over the same Fiscals. (Risk Factor 1)
Customer concentration: revenue from the top ten customers accounted for 57.59%, 55.90% and 61.65% of revenue from sale of products in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively. (Risk Factor 5)

Supplier concentration with no long-term supply agreements: purchases from the top ten suppliers accounted for 25.50%, 18.41% and 50.33% of total expenses in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively; raw materials are procured through purchase orders rather than long-term agreements. Geographic concentration of assets: all manufacturing facilities (Rau, Pithampur, and the commissioned Ujjain and Mhow facilities) and all dedicated R&D centres are located in the state of Madhya Pradesh, and all revenues are generated from manufacturing operations conducted there. (Risk Factor 6)

Certain Subsidiaries have incurred losses during the last three Fiscals and certain Subsidiaries have reported negative net worth in the last three Fiscals. (Risk Factor 57)

Return on Net Worth declined over the disclosed period: 13.90% in Fiscal 2024, 11.79% in Fiscal 2025 and 9.48% in Fiscal 2026 (weighted average 10.99%), as certified by M/s. A B M S & Associates, Chartered Accountants, pursuant to certificate dated August 18, 2026. (Basis for Offer Price)

Under-utilisation risk on newly added capacity: the Ujjain Facility and Mhow Facility were only commissioned as of March 31, 2026 with R&D and pilot-scale operations started, and the Company may face delays in optimising their performance. (Risk Factor 37)
Complex injectables offering is not yet commercialised and the Company may not be successful in commercialising it, notwithstanding its stated focus on that vertical. (Risk Factor 22)
CDMO business commenced only in 2025 and is subject to risks including those of a newly commenced line of business. (Risk Factor 26)

Equity Shares have been issued during the preceding 12 months at prices that may be lower than the Offer Price. (Risk Factor 13)
Certain manufacturing facilities are not located on land owned by the Company, which holds only leasehold rights. (Risk Factor 35)
Some Promoters and Directors may have interests in entities in businesses similar to that of the Company. (Risk Factor 24)

overview.business_model: The company manufactures and sells corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs - a portfolio of over 60 APIs including Hydrocortisones, Betamethasones, Methylprednisolones, Progesterones, Estrogens and Testosterones - produced using fermentation and multi-step complex chemical reactions at backward-integrated, regulator-approved plants (US FDA, WHO-GMP, EU-GMP). Revenue is earned from (a) sale of APIs, (b) sale of complex injectables and (c) CDMO services for specialty pharmaceutical and nutraceutical companies. In Fiscal 2026 sale of APIs was Rs 8,350.05 million (96.07% of revenue from operations), complex injectables Rs 330.50 million (3.80%) and CDMO services Rs 10.94 million (0.13%), on total revenue from operations of Rs 8,691.49 million. As of March 31, 2026 it served over 200 customers in more than 40 countries (more than 50 domestic and 150 export customers), with 67.04% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations from international markets and 32.96% from domestic markets. Top five products contributed 62.27% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026.

Regulated-market filing estate that is slow to replicate: 43 drug master files with the US FDA and 23 EDQM certificates of suitability as of March 31, 2026 (66 API DMFs/CEPs versus 64 in each of Fiscals 2025 and 2024), US FDA approval held 16 years at Rau and 13 years at Pithampur, EU-GMP by Regierung von Oberbayern at both, and the RHP's own statement that 'We have not received any critical observations from global regulators in course of their inspections over the last three Fiscals.'

Margin expansion alongside deleveraging: EBITDA margin 24.48% (FY2024) to 27.26% (FY2025) to 26.59% (FY2026) on FY2026 EBITDA of Rs 2,319.73 million; total debt cut from Rs 5,409.23 million to Rs 3,879.14 million and cash from operations recovered from Rs 472.56 million (FY2025) to Rs 1,745.93 million (FY2026) against net worth of Rs 11,586.41 million.

Stated volume leadership in a narrow molecule set - global volume share of 38.2% in corticosteroid and 23.8% in steroidal-hormone APIs in Fiscal 2026, and product-level shares of 80.1% Hydrocortisone, 76.4% Testosterone and 76.0% Methylprednisolone - with the caveat that every one of these figures is attributed to the Frost & Sullivan report the Company itself commissioned and paid for (engagement letter dated June 19, 2026; Risk Factor 55), not to independent data.

Capacity for the next leg is already built and paid for: Rs 7,986.11 million invested over three Fiscals took fermentation capacity from 300 KL to 700 KL (Ujjain 400 KL, investment Rs 4,794.58 million) and added 20 million double chamber vials per annum at Mhow (investment Rs 3,919.19 million), both stated as commissioned as of March 31, 2026, so growth does not depend on new Offer money.

Customer base broadened while concentration eased: over 200 customers in more than 40 countries as of March 31, 2026, with top-ten customers down to 57.59% of revenue from sale of products in Fiscal 2026 from 61.65% in Fiscal 2024; R&D team of 156 scientists and engineers (117 masters, 10 PhDs) across three Indore centres, R&D spend Rs 296.95 million in Fiscal 2026.

Insurance cover of Rs 17,961.00 million against insurable assets of Rs 13,460.21 million (133%) as at March 31, 2026, with no claim exceeding coverage in the last three Fiscals; CARE A+ on the Company's long-term bank facilities at December 31, 2025.

products.title: Products (RHP)
products.body:
- "We have a robust portfolio comprising 48 DMFs and CEPs for corticosteroid APIs, which are universally applied extensively in critical care setups, as well as across chronic therapeutic areas such as respiratory, dermatology, pain management, oncology and gynecology." (Business Operations – APIs, Business chapter, RHP pp.218-251). Items listed are the corticosteroid molecules the RHP itself names in its Strengths / portfolio-depth tables; the RHP does not print a full SKU list.
- "We have a robust portfolio comprising 18 DMFs and CEPs for steroidal-hormone APIs, which are universally applied for hormone replacement." (Business Operations – APIs). Portfolio-level: "a robust product portfolio of over 60 corticosteroid and steroidal-hormone APIs" (Overview) and, in the capacity-table notes, "Our Company has a portfolio of more than 50 products, each with a distinct and different manufacturing cycle time." Both figures are printed as such; they are not reconciled by the RHP.
- "We have a pipeline of classical fermentation and differentiated APIs including anti-infectives, anti-fungals, immunosuppressants, enzymes and anti-parasitics. Using our fermentation infrastructure, we manufacture recombinant protein like GLP-1 and Insulins." (Business Operations – APIs). "We have already launched fermentation-based APIs such as Mupirocin and Serratiopeptidase, among others" (Strategies).
- "we intend to commercialise our conjugated estrogen products in the dosage form of a vaginal cream and oral tablets"; "one of the few companies globally to have successfully developed a complex API with 82 US FDA mandated components". Not yet a revenue line in the FY2026/FY2025/FY2024 vertical table.
- "As of March 31, 2026, we are developing DCV products under the Section 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway of the U.S. Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act, in addition to two developed DCV products. As of the date of this Red Herring Prospectus, we have achieved proof of concept for DCBs and DCSs and are presently conducting stability testing for DCBs."
- Business Operations – CDMO services. No contract values are printed for any of these arrangements. "We commenced our CDMO business in Fiscal 2025."
- Strategies chapter: "we intend to build on this foundation by introducing additional high-value, low-volume APIs in niche therapeutic areas, as well as speciality ingredients such as Vegan Vitamin D3 and Algal based Docosa Hexanoic Acid (DHA)." Intended, not a disclosed revenue line.
- Printed in both the Business chapter (Strengths) and Risk Factor 1. The RHP does not name the individual top-five or top-ten products or give per-product revenue, so no per-product revenue split can be populated.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration: "Our broad capabilities are enabled by conversion of commodity plant-based derivative inputs (farm/microbe-to-pharmacy approach) and work with diverse microbial strains such as bacteria, fungi, yeast and algae to convert into high value steroid and hormonal pre-cursors. This supports backward integration and underpins our 'farm/microbe-to-pharmacy' approach. This integration allows us to make strategic, cost-effective 'make versus buy' decisions for key starting materials (KSMs) for over 80% of our products by revenue, thereby reducing external dependence for sourcing intermediates from other geographies. We are among the few backward-integrated Indian and global manufacturers capable of producing in-house corticosteroid and hormone precursors, as of March 31, 2026. (Source: F&S Report)" Fermentation capabilities span four modalities: (i) biotransformation of soy-derived sterols to corticosteroid and hormone pre-cursors, with in-house control over each step from raw material to final API production; (ii) classical fermentation for pipeline APIs; (iii) recombinant protein expression technologies for GLP-1 and Insulins; and (iv) precision fermentation and synthetic biology for nutraceuticals and food applications. Forward integration: "We have strategically invested in forward integration to complement our API and fermentation strengths with capabilities in technically complex injectables. Our complex injectables platform is centered on double chamber vials (DCVs) and differentiated drug device combinations, including double chamber bags (DCBs), and double chamber syringes (DCSs). We are one of the first generics companies globally to successfully develop DCV through backward integration, by relying on in-house materials and not imports, for Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate injection and Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate." Residual external dependence: "Our principal raw materials include phytosterols and certain fermentation-based and semi-synthetic intermediates, as KSMs for our APIs. We procure such raw materials from our suppliers based on purchase orders" and "do not enter into any long-term agreements with our suppliers." Raw material sourcing (Rs. million and % of total expenses, Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024): sourced domestically 781.35 (11.00%) / 915.79 (15.04%) / 785.62 (12.84%); raw material imports 1,868.82 (26.32%) / 1,197.36 (19.67%) / 3,275.61 (55.43%), of which United States of America 59.77 (0.84%) / 39.10 (0.64%) / 20.02 (0.34%), China 1,695.24 (23.88%) / 1,024.32 (16.82%) / 3,119.82 (52.79%), and other countries (Singapore, Malaysia and Germany) 113.81 (1.60%) / 133.94 (2.20%) / 135.76 (2.30%). "While we are in the process of increasing fermentation capacity through our commissioned Ujjain Facility to reduce our reliance on external raw materials, we continue to source some of our raw materials from third parties." Investment: "We have invested over Rs. 7,986.11 million in setting up additional capacities and capabilities in both API and complex injectables manufacturing over the last three Fiscals." Sustainability: renewable energy (solar and wind), carbon-neutral bio-briquettes, zero liquid discharge systems and re-use of treated water across all sites.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Two statements are printed, and the RHP does not reconcile them. (1) MD&A, section 'SEASONALITY OF BUSINESS' (affirmative nil): "Our business is not seasonal in nature." (2) Risk Factors, CDMO risk factor, forward-looking: "Seasonality - We expect to in future experience an increase in shipments made to our customers in the last quarter of our financial year from January to March as this corresponds to the start of the financial year for most of our customers who operate on a calendar year basis, where they typically conduct their capacity planning for the year and purchase more quantities of product from us resulting in generally more invoices raised in the relevant quarter, or an increase in the value of these invoices. As a result of such seasonal fluctuations, our revenue and cash flow from operations may fluctuate due to the increase in demand for our products during the fourth quarter of our financial year. Further, as a result of the above, our quarter on quarter financial results may not be comparable or a meaningful indicator of our future performance." This second statement is expressly about the CDMO business and is framed as an expectation for the future, not a historical pattern.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Any reduction in demand for APIs, and our top products in particular, or disruption in production, could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- In addition to manufacturing API products that we sell, we offer our services as a contract development and manufacturing organisation (“CDMO”) for specialty pharmaceutical and nutraceutical companies.
- As of March 31, 2026, we served over 200 customers across more than 40 countries.
- This facility, which has been established with an investment of ₹ 3,919.19 million as of March 31, 2026, is a key part of our strategy to enter high-value, technology-driven complex injectables.
- For further information, see “Our Business – Strategies - Commercialize complex injectables through differentiated drug device combinations” on page 236. (2) We commenced our CDMO business in Fiscal 2025 and have commissioned the Ujjain Facility, which we intend to use as a base for non-pharmaceutical CDMO opportunities going forward.
- Our revenues from the sale of API products may decline as a result of increased market acceptance for our competitors’ products instead of ours, breakthroughs in the development of more effective or popular alternative products, regulatory action, pricing pressures, fluctuations in the demand for our products, or disruptions in the supply of our products.
- We face competition both within our API manufacturing business and in our role as a CDMO, which we have recently commenced.
- An inability to compete effectively may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.” and “- We may be subject to pricing pressure from our customers, which could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.” on pages 36 and 60, respectively.
